ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $6.27 Ryde voucher (NS-7) to the rider for the 4.45 km of unexcused off-route metered distance; no account flag against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
SAFETY SCREEN: I read the rider's complaint, the driver's Chat #1 (F8) and the driver's post-trip statement (F10). The complaint is a fare/routing grievance ("the fare was higher than the estimate"), the chat is a route question, and the statement is a factual claim. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern = none and no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation arises [F8][F10][SAFE-1].

ROUTE DEVIATION: The trace settles that one off-route segment exists (18:34–18:45, 5.53 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.08 km, +4.45 km) [F3][RD-1]. Under RD-1 the driver must take the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause, and an unexplained deviation breaches that duty [F1][F3][RD-1].

EXEMPTIONS: RD-4 fails on the code-checked incident screen — no traffic incident was recorded near the optimal route in the trip window, and a lone speed band is corroboration only, so the Kampong Bahru Road band 2 record cannot exempt the replaced stretch [F11][F14][RD-4]. RD-3 does not apply: no stop, and no rider-named place, appears in the segment [F8][RD-3].

CONSENT: The only chat message is the driver's own 18:30 question, "mind if I go round via Zion Road?" [F8]; the record holds one message, timestamped, with no rider reply [F9]. RD-5 requires a rider-authored message sent before the segment began (18:34), and the driver's post-trip claim of "no objection" is a statement, not consent [F10][RD-5]. The 18:30 question does precede the segment, so the rule's timing condition is met — but RD-5's consent condition is not. Even if the record had shown a rider assent, it would only be a specific named-road agreement ("via Zion Road"), and nothing in the table ties the driven segment to Zion Road (no stop there, no message placing the car there, no road name for the driven path), which would make the scope undetermined under G13 [F3][F8][RD-5]. That undetermined point changes neither the amount nor any account flag, so it does not force an escalation: on the consent element as actually recorded — a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment — the segment counts.

AMOUNT: RydeTAXI is metered, so the off-route kilometres entered the fare directly. The trace formula uses this trip's per-km rate, distance fare ÷ distance km = $18.37 ÷ 13.03 km = $1.4098/km [F4][F7]. Refund = 4.45 km × $1.4098/km = $6.274 → $6.27 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The remaining 0.85 km of billed excess ($7.47 − $6.27), the corridor/jitter mileage and the fare-excess outside the segments are expressly non-refundable under RD-2 [F4][RD-2]. The metered waiting item of $0.11 follows RD-3(c) and stays, and there is no surge and no FARE-1 add-on [F5][F6][F7][FARE-1].

ACCOUNT ACTION: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days to send the account for review; the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes (the one upheld matter is not a route case), so no flag_account arises [F17][RD-6]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS, fare, chat and profile records settle every element this ruling needs [F3][F4][F7][F8][F9].

segment_findings.reason: The only chat message is the driver's own 18:30 proposal to go via Zion Road, sent before the segment began at 18:34 [F8][F9], but RD-5 requires a RIDER message of agreement before the segment; no rider reply exists in the record, and the driver's statement of 'no objection' is a post-trip claim and not consent [F10][RD-5]. RD-3 does not apply because no rider-named stop was made [F8][RD-3], and RD-4 fails because no incident on the replaced stretch was recorded and a lone speed band cannot exempt [F11][F14][RD-4]. The segment is therefore an unexcused deviation.

rejected_claims.reason: Timing is satisfied but consent is not: the 18:30 question precedes the 18:34 segment [F8][F3], yet RD-5 requires the rider's own agreement before the segment and the record contains only the driver's message with no rider reply [F8][F9][RD-5], so the proposal cannot exempt the segment.

Correctly concedes no exemption for F3: with no fact tying the driven segment to Zion Road, any named-road agreement could not cover it [F8][F3][RD-5]; the record's complete chat with no rider agreement makes the segment count rather than resolve in the driver's favour.

The driver's profile (5.2-year account, 4.91 rating, 347 trips, one non-route upheld dispute) cannot decide the case: profile facts never outweigh the GPS and fare records showing +5.3 km against a 7.7 km optimal route and +4.45 km on the segment [F1][F3][F17][RD-2].

No account flag follows: RD-6 requires a prior upheld ROUTE dispute in the 90-day window and the driver's profile records route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F17][RD-6], so this case does not make the breach 'repeated'.

The ceiling is confirmed, not enlarged: the billed excess is 5.30 km / $7.47 while only the 4.45 km of F3 is attributable to an unexcused segment, and RD-2 expressly leaves the residual kilometre and fare-excess outside the segments unrecovered [F3][F4][RD-2].
